data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 performance for 15-year-old students in Hungary across mathematics, reading, and science, and reports trends relative to earlier PISA cycles (notably 2018 and 2015). It states that students took two two-hour subject tests with different item combinations across students, and that results are released as official performance estimates with uncertainty (95% confidence intervals). For Hungary, average performance in mathematics declined compared to 2018, while reading and science were about the same as in 2018; science was higher than in 2015 and part of the earlier decline was reversed. The factsheet also reports proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2 and top levels 5–6) and subgroup patterns such as socioeconomic divides (ESCS) and gender differences. It does not present any student-level predictive modeling, algorithmic comparison, or explicit PV/missing-data handling procedures in the provided text.
